Since last year, me and my room mates have enjoyed drinking and playing this game together. The last update however, made the game significantly less fun. It was so bad, that we actually put the game down after only fifteen minutes. This is the shortest that we have ever played the game. All in all, the latest update is a very large step backward.

The first of my three biggest complains, is that that knockouts are totally broken. You can't knock people out anymore. If you hear the *crack* sound when you knock someone out, they're back up within a second. This takes all the fun out of watching helplessly as someone clumsily tries to throw you over a railing. It's almost impossible to even throw someone out now in the wrestling ring arena now. The only way we were able to get someone out, was when the game glitched, and the person trying to pick up someone knocked out flew into the air.

The second, is that the climbing mechanics are practically nonexistant. A large portion of the game's appeal to me and my room mates, was trying to grab onto someone climbing a wall, and pulling them off. The new climbing is awful. We used to be able to scale the wall in the train arena to avoid being hit by the train, but you can't even get that high anymore. Even worse, if you try to continue to climb after running out of "climbing stamina", you slide back down the wall. On a similar note, it appears that the grip strength has been reduced as well. This has also been very frustrating.

The third issue, is that the lives no longer appear on screen anymore. It turns out that if you hit the back button, you can see them, but that's extremely inconvenient.

As much as it pains me, I can't recommend this game until the developers have either fixed these issues, or rolled back to the previous version. This really is a great game, and the developers have been on top of updating it and adding new levels. I would still reccomend this game, but I hope that this negative vote is enough to get the attention of the developers.

This game was absolutely amazing when I first played it over a year ago. I really feel like the blend of glitchy physics and simplistic gameplay on levels breakable in ways that shouldn't have been possible absolutely captured lightning in a bottle.

Since then, however, I feel every update has been loosening the lid and letting a little bit of that magic slip out to the point where the remaining charm exists solely in the mild amusement from watching increasingly Raving Rabbids / Minions-esque characters slap each other a little bit.

It makes me feel as though Boneloaf had a very specific vision for this game - one that is unfortunately wildly superceded by the earlier releases. Trying to reign in the out of control physics and removing things like Waves and Race mode - tweaking the climbing system and dumbing down the options available to you for game customisation (off the top of my head, infinite grip) has truly killed the fun I had in this game.

This, in combination with wildly simplifying the levels has turned this game into nothing but a reminder of the great fun it used to be. Back in the day, it wasn't uncommon to uppercut someone onto an airvent attached to the ceiling before knocking it down in an attempt to climb up there with them, or dropkick someone across the room into a well-timed sausage-hole. Now, it's unlikely that anything will happen other than two characters wildly flailing until one falls over followed by the survivor dumping the fallen off an edge.

TL;DR: What was once up in the pinnacle of couch competitive games has unfortunately slipped into disappointment.

Would no longer recommend, but it was fun while it lasted.

Seeing this game in my library always makes me a bit sad, as this game was once the go-to game for my friends and I, and we had tons of fun playing it, but despite the game being a decent game in it's current state, it's not the same as it was back then and it's history makes it impossible for me to recommend.

When I originally purchases this game back in 2014, the game was fairly barebones (as many early access games are), but my friends and I had a blast brawling and goofing off in what was there, and we were excited for the full release of the game (which promised to include many more features, like additional maps and a story mode). The game had a very large number of bugs and it was quite common for a match to end in a janky, broken mess, but we were reassured that these would be patched quickly and the full game would be released soon.

Over the years of owning this game, it went through an astounding number of revisions and changes, and while new maps and costumes were slowly added to the game, most of the changes were to the mechanics or the engine of the game. This was quite frustrating, as not only were the pretty serious bugs with the game rarely fixed, but the changes meant that things like climbing or knocking other players out were constantly changing, and frequently needing to relearn how to perform these actions (or why things weren't working like they did previously) was frustrating.

When the game was finally released in 2017, it was noticeably absent of features that had been promised many years before, like a story mode (and mention of the features had been silently removed from the store page), but my friends and I were still hopeful that we would enjoy this game from then on, as the bugs would hopefully be almost entirely eradicated and the game would no longer be in a cycle of repeated rework which changed how the game worked. Unfortunately, neither of those proved to be true, and they continued to make sweeping changes to the game, and still struggled to solve many bugs (although to their credit, the game did get somewhat less unstable as time went on). Although it seems they may have stopped making large sweeping changes to this game for now, I simply don't trust them given my history with them, and despite all the changes in the past, there are still incredibly game-breaking bugs in this game, such as clipping through objects or the map, players dying or surviving inexplicably, or broken object interactions causing objects to suddenly accelerate in a random direction at an incredibly high speed.

[b]TL;DR[/b] While my friends and I had a lot of fun playing this game in the past, and it's a game you very well could enjoy, there have been repeated sweeping changes to the game over the years which failed to deliver promised content or fix critical bugs which still exist in this game today, and as such, I simply can't recommend it.

I've been following Gang Beasts since around 2013 when it was just a twinkle in the eye of a couple of friends on IndieDB, even before the pre-alpha.

Since then this game has seen many transitions, even stepping backwards many times in the gameplay department but never lost it's touch. That is, until they decided to develop a PS4 version as well and then replace the PC version with it. Since then, the game has gone MAJORLY down hill. It's lost almost all of it's charm, by that I mean the way it USED to play. You could do a lot of stupid and silly things, I don't think Gang Beasts was ever meant to be a fighter but more so a silly brawler. By tightening up the controls and trying to make the game better they've made it worse in many ways. They also introduced a stamina system a while back that contributed to me not wanting to play it simply because there was no TOGGLE for it. Sometimes I just wanted to climb the stages for fun without some stamina limitation in my way. They also removed a lot of the "bugs" which weren't really bugs but more so just stupid things that made the game a little more fun.

They've tried to make the fighting more streamlined but they've honestly made it worse, the character controls are still clunky but the character tries to respond quicker to your inputs which leads to a lot of frustration, they also changed the grab scheme too, now you can't even reach up high to grab, you can only reach waist height, climbing while faster now feels worse thanks to some of the mentioned issues. You also cannot grab someone and jump now, they'll automatically let go and I have no idea why they did this, it's stupid and just removes yet another bit of charm the game had. The game has always looked decent but with the PS4 patch they tried to make it look nicer and instead of doing that they killed performance completely. Gang Beasts was always kind of heavy on the system for no reason but the PS4 patch shot it through the roof. The menu is also still very clunky, the only positive out of all of this is the updated costume customizer, that's it and even then, the jelly dudes look worse than they did before some how.

The game's biggest problem is the gameplay/controls, since trying to "fix" them they've completely broken what was fun about this game. They tried to make it more skill based but it didn't work at all, often times now my hits don't connect at all and I'm seemingly always being one punch KO'd by AI instantly, you can't sprint and then jump anymore like you could before, kicking barely works, the dive kick is fairly useless considering how low you jump, the head butt now leads to more self KO's than anything so it's also mostly useless and grabbing is just awful, your character will grab everything but the thing/person you're trying to grab, it was a little tricky pre-PS4 patch but now it's just absolutely God awful. Devs also talked about moving the game into a more general direction back before it was picked up by a publisher, they talked about doing a lot of the things that Human Fall Flat has done, races/obstacle courses and big open spaces, but they seem to have completely dropped this aspect of the game.

So yeah, almost everything that made Gang beasts feel like Gang Beasts is now gone. I hardly enjoyed the last few hours I've put into Gang Beasts since the PS4 update. It just doesn't feel good or feel like the game I originally paid for. I HATE giving negative reviews, I can usually find a good reason to give a positive review but ultimately, Gang Beasts has let me down hard specially for being such a hugely loyal fan for so many years. I expected a lot more.

I bought this game years ago while it was still in early access; the game trailer made it look silly and fun so I thought it would be a good game for me and my son. Let me tell you - I have never laughed so hard playing a game before, nor had I heard my son laugh so much at a game. We would play for hours upon hours. There was the odd game crash because it was in early access, but any other bugs usually just made  you laugh more, like your character slowly stretching apart and flying into the air, or getting launched at mach 3 across the map and slamming into the wall. If you had asked me then if you should get this game I would've said yes in a heartbeat, even for $40.00, I'd say buy the game.

They eventually fixed the game crashes and loads of other bugs which was appreciated. However fast forward to now and after multiple new updates the game has improved cosmetically, but the gameplay has gotten much worse. I don't play it anymore and honestly when I come back after a couple months to see if the latest patch has improved things it just makes me sad, because it never does play like it used to and it just reminds me how good this game used to be. 

These are the 4 main reasons why I feel it's not the fun game it used to be:

1) Punches simply don't land well anymore. 

There was always a bit of luck involved when it comes to who would knock out who, but now you can hit left/right punch over and over and over and have nothing happen, even when you throw some head butts in too.

2) Even if you do finally get a knock out, they're back up within less than a couple seconds. 

You have to get successive knockouts in order for the other player to actually stay down for a lengthier amount of time. This might be okay if punching didn't work so poorly now.

3) You used to be able to break out of grapples more reliably. 

If someone grabs you, you used to be able to spam jump and after a few jumps you'd break out and leap slightly away from the other player. Now you can spam it all you want but you're usually just going to still be stuck to the other player for as long as they keep holding grab. I suppose this ups the "silly" factor since it makes kamikazee type plays more common given that you usually can't get away from someone grabbing you and jumping off the edge, but that gets old quickly when you actually want to try to play to win and not draw.

4) You used to be able to climb pretty much all surfaces very easily. You could grab a wall and spam jump to get all the way to the top.

This would make for hilarious games where you'd be chasing each other to all edges of the map and trying to grab someone's leg to pull them off the wall. I understand they likely changed this to avoid griefing in online matches, but man if they only could've at least kept it allowed in local play.

There are other minor issues but those 4 things I feel are the main reason why this game is not what it used to be. The problem is that if you've never played Gang Beasts before, you could buy the game and still have fun for a bit because it is so wacky, so I can see why this still sometimes gets positive reviews from new players or Youtubers that only play for a couple hours with friends. But if you were to ask those same people after say 10, 20 hours of gameplay, I suspect they would be getting bored with it already. It's really disappointing for someone who's played since the beginning and knows that before there used to be an actual competitive game underneath the wackiness, one that actually played pretty well.

At this point I would guess that the developers have made their money and are focusing on making a new game by now. But if you devs are reading, I would change this review to be positive in a microsecond if you fixed punching, grapple breaks, and just added some game customization options. Let me decide how long knock outs last in my match, how many punches it takes to K.O., how much stamina players get, etc. 

I put a lot of hours into this game, here's hoping it goes back to the game it used to be at its peak.

I bought this game when it was first put on early access (September, 2014). When the final release dropped I was mostly confused. During its development cycle it had a focus on being like 90s arcade cabinets artistically, with a rocking main theme (Legacy), and a VHS style main menu (0.4.0). The design was set-and-stone throughout development, but out of nowhere they replaced the music with pop-like EDM, and no clear artistic vision appears in the game anymore. I was confused, but considering the last build before final release was 0.7.5-ish I had a strong feeling it was rushed out.

Visually, the final release is at-points-upgraded (textures) but most-points-downgraded. Everything in the game got the standard metallic Unity shader slapped onto it, so now everything has a basic gloss effect that makes it look cheap. The game used to have a simple, colorful, toy design that didn't rely on gloss and looked good on it's own.

Content-wise, there wasn't much added over the 4-year development span. In fact, a lot was removed. The pre-alpha builds (that you can still download somewhere) had a tutorial, sandbox, and a gamemode called Streets resembling a side-scrolling beat-em-up, that was replaced with the clunky, unbalanced Waves mode we have today. The first beta builds (0.2.0 era) were the most experimental-- a Race gamemode with designs resembling racing game-shows (Ex. Wipeout), a gamemode called Break inspired by the car smashing segments of old Street Fighter titles that was mainly meant to toy with the physics of the game, and it gave players the debug menu, which let them play with various objects, gravitational forces, a day-and-night cycle, and even control AI! There are some alternate gamemodes present now, but the Football mode is a clear demonstration of how poorly the characters control, and Waves demonstrates how under-polished the AI and combat mechanics are.

The most that was added to Gang Beasts during development were a lot of the maps; Buoy, Blimp, Towers, Chutes, and Elevators, but all of these maps, including older maps, faced multiple redesigns-- some of which ended up resembling their original counter-parts, anyway. This became a reoccurring distraction for Boneloaf as a result of poor planning.

In various articles, the devs would talk about bringing Streets back, and even making a sort of Campaign with boss fights (I can't find anything on the campaign bit). This was never put in. There were prototype gamemodes in the game's files for CTF and KoTH gamemodes, both not present (CTF was accidentally released once and then removed). They even showed off a ball-pit stage that was never put in.

I once cracked open the game's files myself and found reference to some kind of boat mechanic. Though, I have no idea what it could be referring to, and I never snapped this.

Now, through being disappointed with the development of this game, there's also a problem with communication from the developers, Boneloaf. They like to take long hiatuses and not tell anyone anything for months. For example, just a few days ago they released an update after not saying or doing anything for six months. They announced the 0.2.0 beta 3 months after the last Legacy build, delayed it to the next day, STILL didn't post it and didn't say anything until the end of April when they did post it. 

What I'm saying is they take their sweet time and stay quiet-- now, that's not a bad thing by far! It must mean they put a lot of time into keeping us entertained, right? Well, the thing is, the game's been roughly the same for a long time, adding minimal content through each update and focusing on fixing bugs that most people won't even witness. The problem with content in this game started when they decided to shift gears from couch party to multi-couch party. Since Boneloaf started working on the online multiplayer they've been putting more time adding to that experience than adding to the WHOLE experience. I believe we could have had Streets, Bosses, CTF, KoTH, and other cool modes and maps, but many players wanted an online feature, and I think that totally compromised the development of Gang Beasts.

The recent update added a new map to the game and a few costumes. It took six months to make one map and a few costumes. The only way I'd play this game again is if I could play the 0.2.0 era builds. They were glitchy as hell, but they compensated by being chaotic and experimental. Current Gang Beasts isn't fun-- it's an under-polished missed opportunity. I could play old Gang Beasts for hours, now I can't even play for 20 minutes without getting bored. I can't recommend this game in its current state, and I wish the devs focused on couch party content rather than online multiplayer.

I remember finding this game in a very early build, pre-steam release. It was very unpolished and obviously had a long way to go before it was finshed, but it was stupidly fun to mess around with and even better in local multiplayer mode. The mechanics were simple and that leant itself pefectly to the kind of game it was trying to be.

Unfortunately, as time has passed, what once made the game fun has become more of an annoyance. The perfect example of this is the grab mechanic. It was once a simple case of hold the trigger and your character holds their arm out. From there you would grab onto anything your hand came into contact with and then you'd release when you were ready. eventually the developers decided to add an auto-target mechanic in which your outstretched arm would actively seek to grab something. The problem with that is, the auto-target rarely targets the object you're actually aiming for. Even with an enemy stood directly in front of you, it's a game of chance as to whether you'll grab them, or a nice chunk of floor at your feet instead.

Even in local multiplayer, the once golden gem of Gang Beasts, the magic has been lost. The fighting has always been drunken and goofy, but in the early builds there was at least a sense of rhythm you could perfect to get good at knocking each other out. Now, fighting has devolved into mindlessly spamming three different attack buttons and hoping enough of them will land. Any attempt to 'skill' the system results in you being knocked out flat. It's still funny, for sure, but it's only so long before someone endds up frustrated because they can't figure it out.

It's been such a shame to see this game form from an unpolished goldmine into a well presented mess. Some early builds are still available and I would advise anyone try to seek them out before buying this game.

[h1]As of writing this review, Gang Beasts is still in development.[/h1]

CONS:
[*] No online multiplayer [i]yet[/i].
[*] Wonky control scheme with mouse and keyboard.
[*] Some low-end machines may struggle with certain levels.
[/list]

PROS:
[*] Absurdly fun to play.
[*] To play with friends, you have to be with them, in person, together.
[*] Variety of hazardous levels, large and small.
[*] Great costumes and color choices for your hero.
[*] Ludicrously fun to play.
[*] Controller friendly.
[*] Laugh so hard that your stomach hurts
[*] Really a lot of fun to play
[/list]

[b]Objective[/b]
The game play is great. The objective is simple: kill your opponents. There are plenty of hazards which aid you in your quest. There are meat grinders, there are falls from sky scrapers, there are subway trains. Beat up your opponents and throw them to their doom! This is all carried out in a wonderfully goofy world populated with strangely dressed jello people who make silly noises and giggle at the misfortune of their opponents. It's incredible. 

[b]Control Scheme[/b]
I play with an Xbox 360 Controller. The default button scheme includes the left stick for movement, A/B/X/Y/LB/RB for control of various body parts. All buttons seem to have two functions: one action for a tap, and another for a hold. In the default scheme, LB and RB control the left and right arms respectively. Tapping punches, holding attempts to grasp whatever is at the end of the player's reach. This is helpful for grabbing and holding opponents. Couple this with Y which elevates the arms, and you can grab and lift an opponent over your head. Additionally, you can kick, headbutt, jump, sit, lay forward, lay backward, and many other combinations like jump kicking or climbing.

[b]A Note to Prospective Players[/b]
While I wholly endorse this game and have had loads of fun playing with my friends, I recognize that not everyone has the option to regularly get together with a group of players in one place and play games. If you are the kind of person who can not easily and frequently get together with a few friends to play, I would caution that you wait until online multiplayer is completely finished. Multiplayer Beta is currently active! Find out how to join [url=https://dodistribute.com/access/knof3oKvFd/]here[/url]. If you are in a position to be able to regularly get together with some friends and you want to laugh until you puke, check out this game.

Gang Beast used to be a fun game when it first came out. After a patch, the game isn't fun anymore as all the stuff you used to do before is either taken out or much harder to do. Gang Beasts is a fun little brawler with a few different gamemodes and some over the top maps. Hanging from a skyscraper, or on top of a moving truck or a flaming incinerator, Nothing is too crazy.

The game is really enjoyable with friends, But the gameplay is not really skill based, The controls are so wonky, It is actually hard to hit people, Very competitive players might find it annoying because it is almost luck based. The goal is to throw all the other players off the map, You can lift people above your head, If you knock them out beforehand they go overboard pretty easy.

The controls are pretty simple, You can jump, Grab, Kick, Punch, Lift and Run, It reminds me a lot of Human Fall Flat, Same wonky controls, Only here we fight instead of reach exits. There are a bunch of gamemodes, You can play Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Soccer, Or waves against AI.

I especially like the levels, They went way over the top, And I like that, Crazy levels make for crazy fights, There are levels where you hang from a few containers, levels on top of a billboard, levels on top of driving trucks and even levels on exterior elevators.

I personally do not care about the soccer and waves gamemodes, Soccer is too wonky, But is kinda ok, Waves is just way too hard, The AI won't go down easy. The multiplayer battles is where the fun is, You can play it with u to 4 players Online and Locally or a mix of the 2.

You can also heavily customize the characters, there are thousands of combinations to dress your character. There are even some familliar faces like Rick and Morty, The graphics are nice, It is a low poly kind of style, And the game runs well on Linux

Overall I think it is a great game, Sure the controls are wonky, And personally I would have done this different, but It is kinda part of the game, It adds the randomness and also gives your friends a chance to win. I have to give the game an 8.

Gang Beasts is at its best as a novelty party game.  With the right group of friends this physics-based jelly people wrestling is a blast.  Check out some videos of it on youtube.  If you laugh your head off and are desperate to play it with friends then get it.  The fighting is brilliant, and experimenting with all the different combinations of wobbly break dance fighting will earn some big laughs, and plenty of happy shouting when you throw your mate into the grinder and watch him (or her) attempt a fruitless escape.

Its a bit content-light right now, but there is plenty of fun to be had, and there is loads of stuff on the way.

On to the negative.  Its not a game with a great deal of replay value unless you can organise three player matches.
Single player gets boring quickly after you've seen all there is to see.  You will get a lot of laughs, and certain levels will have earned a soft spot in your heart, but right now there isn't much to do past the first 45 minutes of play.

Presumably, this replay factor will improve once story mode and more game modes are implemented, but right now its not a game solo fighters will want to spend $20 on.

However if you have a couple of mates keen to play this with you then get on board.  At 40% off its a blast and well worth the money.  It even has the potential to replace Smash Bros as your go to fighting game with friends.
